children: Malaysian palm oil futures edged higher, hovering near MYR 4,900 per tonne after recent weakness, supported by firmer soyoils on China’s Dalian markets and expectations of tighter supplies.
Indonesia’s B50 biodiesel mandate is set to divert more palm oil to domestic use, while El Niño risks could curb output in both Indonesia and Malaysia.

Demand prospects also improved as palm oil imports by top consumer India rose 7% from July to 782,761 tonnes in August, the highest since February, with refiners replenishing stocks ahead of the festival season.
Separately, Malaysia raised its October crude palm oil reference price but kept the export duty at 10%.
However, a stronger ringgit tempered gains, along with weaker crude oil prices amid renewed efforts to ease Middle East tensions.
Market focus now turns to a potential import tariff cut in India, with an official announcement expected soon that could sway demand for Malaysian palm oil.

title: Palm Oil Holds Near MYR 4,900 on Supply Concerns
